name: SXN-smdri127
title: SMDRI series shielded SMD power inductors, 1 µH to 1000 µH, sizes 62 to 127
summary: Wire-wound SMD power inductors with a closed magnetic circuit, in seven sizes from 6.5 × 6.8 × 3.0 mm (SMDRI62) to 12.3 × 12.3 × 8.0 mm (SMDRI127). Values run from 1.0 µH to 1000 µH; parts up to 10 µH are ±30 % (N), larger ones ±20 % (M). Each part has a maximum DCR, a saturation current (inductance down 25 %) and a temperature-rise current (40 °C rise); its rated current is the smaller of the two. Uses named: DC/DC converters, LCD televisions, notebook PCs, portable communication equipment and VTR power supplies.

operation.text: How hot the part runs in service is set by the whole assembly: the circuit, the parts around it, the width and thickness of the copper traces, airflow and any other cooling. It is measured in the finished product.

Use within 12 months, stored at 5 to 40 °C and 35 to 65 % RH or less; past that the terminals may solder poorly. Keep away from corrosive gases (salt, acid, alkali), magnets and magnetic fields. Bare fingers leave oil that harms soldering. Dropping or careless removal can damage parts; bending the terminals hard can break the wire. Do not wash the coils; ask SXN first if cleaning is needed.

Preheat before soldering so that solder and part differ by no more than 150 °C. Rework stays within the specified soldering conditions; overheating can short the part, degrade it or shorten its life. The reflow profile and its heat-endurance test are given in the tables.
Current through the winding warms the part as soon as power is applied; the thermal design leaves room for that rise.
Automotive, medical, military and aerospace uses are to be cleared with SXN sales beforehand.
